subject: Request: signed delivery receipts & ephemeral-token proof-of-delivery for SIEM exports

Subject: Request: signed delivery receipts & ephemeral-token proof-of-delivery for SIEM exports

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the workshop earlier — following up with a formal ask from our compliance and secops teams. For our upcoming private deployment we need two things documented and demonstrated for SIEM exports (Splunk HEC endpoint):

- Signed delivery receipts for each telemetry batch (must include SHA256 batch digest, timestamp, and a signature we can verify).
- Token rotation / proof-of-possession approach: we require short-lived tokens (<=1h) and a way to verify they were issued by the vendor, plus rotation logs for auditing.

Can you send a proposal on how Redwood plans to implement these proofs for VPC/on‑prem deployments (mutual TLS + ephemeral tokens or similar), and a minimal acceptance test we can run? Our audit window is next month, so a sample signed receipt and a short description of the rollover workflow would be ideal.

Attachment: globex-siem-evidence-requirements.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Anna Bryant
Head of Security Integrations
Globex Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Bryant <anna.bryant@globex.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Feb 2028 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: signed delivery receipts & ephemeral-token proof-of-delivery for SIEM exports

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. Looping in Kim and Marissa for the cert/ops details. Below is the proposal in outline form; attaching a flow diagram and a sample signed receipt for quick review.

Summary of approach (production-ready, private deployments):

1) Transport and auth
- Primary: mTLS (mutual TLS) from our telemetry broker to customer HEC endpoint; optional fallback to HTTPS + short-lived JWT if mTLS is not supported.
- Certificates managed by the customer or Redwood depending on procurement: we support both customer-provisioned certs and a Redwood-managed certs workflow.

2) Ephemeral token model
- Tokens are short-lived JWTs signed by Redwood KMS with a 1-hour lifetime by default (configurable down to 15m).
- Token issuance is recorded in a tamper-evident audit log (append-only) containing issuer id, requestor id, issuance time, TTL, and a signing key id. Logs are exportable to your SIEM on demand.

3) Signed delivery receipts (proof-of-delivery)
- Each telemetry batch (we chunk by event count or time window) is hashed (SHA256) and a receipt is generated: receipt fields = {batch_id, sequence_start, sequence_end, sha256_digest, utc_timestamp}.
- Receipt is signed using an HMAC-SHA256 keyed with a per-deployment secret; we can also provide an RSA signature if you require asymmetric verification.
- Receipts include a flow_id and monotonic sequence for replay detection.

4) Proof-of-delivery envelope and verification
- We produce a signed manifest (JSON) for each delivery attempt and persist the manifest in the evidence store for N days (configurable).
- Customer can pull manifests via an authenticated API or Redwood can push the receipt into your SIEM as an indexed event. The manifest contains the signature, cert/key id, issuer fingerprint, and the delivery result (200/4xx/5xx with retry metadata).

5) Acceptance test (minimal)
- Step 1: Provide a test HEC endpoint (URL + mTLS cert or token expectation).
- Step 2: Redwood sends three test batches with explicit sequence numbers. Each batch will have a receipt returned and a signed manifest pushed to the endpoint or shared via an S3 presigned URL.
- Step 3: Globex validates SHA256 digests + verifies signature using either HMAC secret we provide out-of-band or by verifying Redwood RSA signature against a public key we publish to the shared drive.

Operational notes and security controls
- Certificate rotation: we propose a 30-day rotation cadence for vendor-managed certs; customer-managed certs use your schedule. We will provide rotation logs and a push-notification of thumbprint changes 72h prior to rotation.
- Replay protection: receipts include a monotonic sequence and timestamp; manifests contain delivery TTL.
- Evidence custody: all signed manifests stored in encrypted object storage and hashed into the audit log. Optional daily signed archive (manifest bundle) can be produced for long-term retention.

Attachments: rdo-telemetry-ephemeral-flow.png (png), signed-receipt-sample.txt (txt)

Requests for you (to finalize test plan):
- Confirm preferred ingest type (mTLS HEC vs HEC over HTTPS with JWT).
- Provide contact for cert exchange (CN and thumbprint) and the endpoint URL for the test.
- Any RSA public key you’d prefer to use for signature verification (if you want asymmetric).

If this looks good I recommend a short canary run (48h) followed by acceptance testing. Kim — can you confirm the rotation notification cadence and whether we can automate thumbprint push to Globex? Marissa — please confirm the evidence retention defaults and how to generate a signed archive on demand.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Wed, Feb 29, 2028 at 10:40 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> If this looks good I recommend a short canary run (48h) followed by acceptance testing.

Hi Anna / Rafael — quick confirmations from the ops side:

- Cert rotation cadence: for Redwood-managed certs we'll do 30-day rotation by default. Notifications: 72h pre-rotation email + manifest push containing new thumbprint. Emergency rekey window: we can do an ad-hoc rotation within 4h for high-severity events.

- Token lifetime: default 1 hour; can be reduced to 15 minutes for high-security tenants.

- Evidence retention: default 90 days in hot store (searchable), 7 years in cold archive on request (signed daily bundles). Archive bundles are SHA256-signed and stored with a signed-index file we can export.

Attached: cert-rotation-plan.csv (csv) — contains proposed rotation windows, notification owners, and playbook IDs.

We'll prepare a short runbook for the canary and share a reproducible test harness (curl + verification script) so your team can validate receipts locally.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Site Reliability Manager — Redwood Inference
